bracket: [Textbook misprint: as printed the question has NO solution. It asks for points on \(x + y - 4 = 0\) at distance \(1\) from \(x + y - 2 = 0\), but those two lines are PARALLEL, so every point of the first is at distance \(\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2}\) from the second and never \(1\). The book's own printed key gives \((3, 1)\) and \((-7, 11)\); both lie on \(x + y - 4 = 0\) AND are at distance exactly \(1\) from \(4x + 3y - 10 = 0\) (\(|12 + 3 - 10|/5 = 1\) and \(|-28 + 33 - 10|/5 = 1\)), so the second line was meant to read \(4x + 3y - 10 = 0\). The key is right; the stem lost a line. Solved against the intended question above.]

[Textbook misprint, answer-affecting: the stem asks for the line \(3\) units BELOW the X-axis, which is \(y = -3\), but the printed solution gives \(y = 3\) — the line 3 units ABOVE it. The correct answer is \(y = -3\).]

[Textbook misprint, answer-affecting: the printed solution asserts \(\tan 30^\circ = \sqrt{3}\). In fact \(\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\), so the line is \(y = \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{3}}\), i.e. \(x - \sqrt{3}y = 0\) — not the printed \(\sqrt{3}x - y = 0\), which is the line of inclination \(60^\circ\).]

[Textbook misprint: the printed stem omits the angle entirely — it reads "the perpendicular makes angle with the positive direction of the X-axis" with no value. Verified at high zoom that the number is genuinely absent rather than clipped. The book's own solution supplies \(30^\circ\), which is the intended question and what is solved above.]

[Textbook misprint (typesetting only, values unaffected): the normal form is printed \(\cos 330^\circ\, x = \sin 330^\circ\, y = 1\) — the \(+\) between the two terms has been set as \(=\); it should read \(x\cos 330^\circ + y\sin 330^\circ = 1\). The closing line also answers \(\theta\) where the question asks for \(\alpha\). The values \(p = 1\), \(\alpha = 330^\circ\) are correct.]
[Textbook misprint (typesetting only): the final line is printed \(x + y - 3 - 0\) — the \(=\) has been set as a minus sign. It should read \(x + y - 3 = 0\).]
[Textbook misprint: the solution states the slope of \(4x + 2y = 7\) as \(m_2 = 2\); it is \(-2\). The book's own next line correctly substitutes \(-2\), so the final answer \(45^\circ\) is right.]

[Textbook misprint (layout, final value unaffected): the book prints the FINAL value \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\) at the HEAD of the working chain, before it is derived, and prints the combined numerator as \(1 - 3\) where it should be \(3 - 1\). The magnitude survives because the expression sits inside \(|\cdot|\), so \(30^\circ\) is correct.]

[Textbook misprint: the penultimate line prints \(3y - 21 = x + 2\); clearing the fraction from \((y - 7) = -\dfrac{1}{3}(x - 2)\) gives \(3y - 21 = -x + 2\). The minus on \(x\) is dropped. The final answer \(x + 3y = 23\) follows from the correct form and is right.]
